tei:titleStmt.tei:title: פיוט לתפילת ערבית
Introductory piyyuṭ for the 'Arvit service, by Aryeh Cohen (translation by Maeera Shreiber)

tei:div.tei:head: Introductory piyyuṭ for the 'Arvit service, by Aryeh Cohen (translation by Maeera Shreiber)

tei:lg.tei:l: Yaaqov initiated the evening prayer;
as it says, “And he came upon a certain place
and stopped there for the night,
for the sun had set” (Genesis 28:11).
And Yaaqov came upon a certain place...
The sun set, without intention
A place with no name, a hidden God
Yaaqov met the one whom he loved
And lay his head on the stone and slept.
You dwelt in me, And our flesh, our souls
Became as one.
Your voice is my prayer, the sparks of holy fire
My lips deceitful, yours utterly silent
If we had only heard, if we had only seen
We would have been in the grips of a nightmare
Our cries ascend
Between the Cherubim
The hour of yearning—twilight
The mouth of the well, the mouth of the donkey
The angels ascend and descend
Yearning and anger gripped
The world is burning, and we are spent.
And where is the owner of the castle?
Silence is praise to you
Once there was thunder, lightning, now silence
Have you just returned to Your Place, and are through?
As I stand before you, I am not silent
As I remember, I am not settled
Nevertheless, for a moment, I will unclench my fists
I will pray to God despite the nightmare
Because truly there is God in this place

tei:note.tei:p: There is a teaching of the Ba’al Shem Tov in Amud Hatefilah (Pillar of Prayer) where the worshipper is described as a shofar blown by God. That is, the breathe and the “voice” belongs to God.
God’s voice comes from between the “Aron” in the Temple. “Between the Cherubim” is a phrase used to describe God’s inner circle, those who are closest.
In Pirqei Avot 5:6 it is said that ten things we were created at twilight, including the mouth of Miriam’s well and the mouth of Bilaam’s jenny.
A midrashic reference to God as responsible for the word. Find, for example, Genesis Rabbah 39:1
In the Talmud, God is described as retreating to a place beyond reach.
”Surely Adonai is present in this place...” (Genesis 28:16)
